clue.text: Catches up with extra drinks

parts.note: over means extra, left in excess
takes means drinks, as in takes tea

explanation.surface: A drinker catches up with friends by ordering more rounds.
explanation.definitionFit: To overtake is to draw level with and pass someone, so it fits catching up.

clue.text: English peer accepts new honour

indicators.note: a piece that accepts another takes it inside itself

parts.note: a peer is a noble, a member of the nobility

explanation.surface: An English lord takes on a new honour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'accepts' puts N inside E plus NOBLE, between the two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: To ennoble someone is to honour them by raising them to the peerage.

clue.text: One harrying soldiers in a defile?

indicators.note: in places the soldiers inside the defile

parts.note: a defile is a narrow pass between hills, here pictured as tor and tor, two rocky hills, either side
men is a common crossword word for soldiers

explanation.surface: Troops are being harassed as they march through a narrow pass.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful picture: a defile is a narrow pass, imagined here as soldiers squeezed between two rocky hilltops; 'in' does the placing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tormentor is someone who harries or persecutes another.

clue.text: Stimulus provided by soup, say, may get a you roaring off

definitions.text: may get a you roaring off

parts.note: a kick is a thrill or stimulus, as in getting a kick out of something
soup is an example of a starter, the first course of a meal

explanation.surface: A bowl of soup gives you a lift and sends you roaring away.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'a' before 'you' looks like a stray word in the printed text. The kickstarter is the pedal that starts a motorbike engine.
explanation.definitionFit: A kickstarter is the pedal that fires a motorcycle engine, sending the rider roaring away.

clue.text: So the reading is correct

definitions.meaning: printed in brackets after a quotation to show an odd wording is really what the original says

explanation.surface: A proofreader confirms that a passage has been read correctly.
explanation.definitionFit: This Latin word means thus and is used to confirm a quotation is reproduced exactly.

clue.text: It's an advantage to declare when run out

indicators.note: out says the letter for run is taken away

parts.note: to assert is to declare
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: In cricket, it pays to declare the innings once a batsman has been run out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when' is a link; 'out' removes R from ASSERT. To declare in cricket is to end an innings by choice; run out is a way of dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is something useful or valuable, an advantage to its owner.

clue.text: The whole of the scripture is appropriate

parts.note: all means the whole of something
OT, the Old Testament, is a body of scripture

explanation.surface: Someone argues that the entire Bible is fitting reading.
explanation.definitionFit: To appropriate funds is to set them aside for a purpose, which is to allot them.

clue.text: Overturned coach on the green causing upset

indicators.note: on places the coach above the green in a down answer
overturned in a down clue says the word for coach is turned upside down, read upwards

parts.note: a coach is a bus
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A coach has rolled over on a village green, causing a stir.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overturned' turns BUS into SUB; 'on' puts it above VERT, the heraldic term for green.
explanation.definitionFit: To subvert is to undermine or overthrow, a sense of upset as a verb.

clue.text: Mounting horses, say, Army team turn scarlet — gosh!

parts.note: TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve
XI, eleven, is a cricket or football team

indicators.note: turn says the word for scarlet is read backwards

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
my! is an exclamation like gosh!

explanation.surface: Army riders go red with embarrassment as they climb onto horses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turn' reverses RED to give DER. TA (Territorial Army) and XI (a side of eleven) are standard abbreviations.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxidermy is the craft of stuffing and mounting animals such as horses for display.

clue.text: Information leading Heather shortly to cheap drug

indicators.note: leading puts the information in front of the heather

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: shortly says the word for heather loses its last letter

parts.note: erica is the botanical name for heather

explanation.surface: A tip-off steers Heather towards an inexpensive medicine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' cuts ERICA to ERIC. The capital on 'Heather' makes it look like a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: A generic is an unbranded drug, sold more cheaply than the branded version.

clue.text: Title fight in booth

parts.note: to call is to name or title something
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: A championship bout is held inside a small booth.
explanation.definitionFit: A callbox is a public telephone booth.

clue.text: Food put forward for consideration

definitions.meaning: a ... can mean the food served, as in keeping a good ...
to ... a motion is to present it for discussion

explanation.surface: A dish is proposed for discussion at a meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both the meals provided at a house and presenting a proposal for debate.

clue.text: Frisky horse had time to win by such a margin

definitions.text: to win by such a margin

indicators.note: frisky suggests lively movement, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A lively horse took its time but still won by a narrow margin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Frisky' shuffles HORSE, HAD and T together.
explanation.definitionFit: In racing, a horse that wins by a nose-length margin is said to win by a short head.

clue.text: Stop during excursion, being unsettled

indicators.note: during puts the stop inside the excursion

parts.note: an outing is an excursion or trip
to stand is to stop still

explanation.surface: A pause during a day trip leaves everyone uneasy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' does the placing. 'unsettled' means not yet paid, like a bill, not upset or uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding bill is one still unpaid, i.e. not yet settled.

clue.text: Eggs fit for Croesus?

indicators.note: fit for here means fitting inside, so the answer sits within the name

explanation.surface: Fish eggs are a delicacy fit for the richest king.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fit for' signals letters sitting inside 'Croesus'. Croesus was a fabulously rich ancient king, and fish roe like caviar is a luxury.
explanation.definitionFit: Roe is the mass of eggs in a female fish.

parts.note: toast is bread browned by heat
a master is an expert

explanation.walkthrough: The capital on 'Browning' suggests the poet, but it is making toast.
explanation.definitionFit: A toastmaster announces the speakers and toasts at a formal dinner.

clue.text: Reduce end of bend before TT race perhaps

indicators.note: before puts that letter ahead of the rest
end of picks out the final letter of bend
perhaps says the letters may come in another order

explanation.surface: Riders slow down for the final bend before the Isle of Man motorcycle race.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns TT RACE into ETRACT. The TT is the famous motorcycle race on the Isle of Man.
explanation.definitionFit: To detract from something is to take away from it, diminishing it.

clue.text: Girl's right to abandon host

indicators.note: to abandon says the letter for right leaves the host

parts.note: a host is an army, as in the heavenly host

explanation.surface: A girl decides it is right to walk out on her host.
explanation.walkthrough: 'host' means a great crowd or army, not someone giving a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, so the definition is by example: it is one girl's name among many.

clue.text: One manual gives it as corundum

indicators.note: gives means yields or bends, so the letters are reshaped

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A handbook explains what corundum is.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gives' shuffles I and MANUAL. 'it as' is link material.
explanation.definitionFit: Corundum is the crystalline mineral form of aluminium oxide.

clue.text: Advice to batsman in accident

definitions.meaning: a cricket call to strike the ball and take a run at once
a road accident where the driver flees the scene

explanation.surface: A batsman is told how to avoid an accident.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a batting instruction and a collision where the driver leaves without stopping.

indicators.note: strange suggests the letters are odd, rearranged

clue.text: Fabulous cricket side with a line protecting the boundary

indicators.note: protecting means surrounding, so the boundary sits inside

parts.note: leg is the leg side of a cricket field
RY, railway, is a line
an end is a boundary or limit

explanation.surface: A cricket team is praised for guarding its boundary rope brilliantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'protecting' does the placing, with 'with' a link. The leg side is one half of a cricket field, and the boundary is read as an end.
explanation.definitionFit: Fabulous originally means belonging to fable or legend, so it matches legendary.
